alabama.law: Alabama has no separate mobile-home park tenancy act. Lot rentals are covered by the general Alabama Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, Code of Alabama Title 35, Chapter 9A, whose definition of dwelling unit includes a manufactured home.
alabama.rent: The general landlord-tenant act does not set a separate lot-rent increase notice period for manufactured-home parks.
alabama.closure: The general landlord-tenant act does not set a park closure or change-of-use notice period, and it does not set a park relocation-assistance duty.
alabama.eviction: Eviction grounds are not a closed park-specific list. Under the general act, a landlord may terminate for material noncompliance with the rental agreement or for failure to pay rent, under Section 35-9A-421.
alabama.link_label: Alabama Legislature - Code of Alabama, Section 35-9A-304

alaska.law: Park tenancies are covered by the Alaska Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, Alaska Statutes 34.03.010 to 34.03.380, which contains specific mobile-home park provisions at AS 34.03.040(c) and AS 34.03.225.
alaska.rent: For a month-to-month tenancy, the landlord must give at least 30 days notice before a rent increase takes effect. A rent increase is treated as ending the agreement at the old rate and offering it at the new rate.
alaska.closure: For a change in use of the park land, affected dwellers or tenants must be given at least 270 days notice, or longer if a valid lease or a municipality requires longer. The quit date must be not earlier than May 1 and not later than October 15, and a municipality may establish a relocation fund to compensate for disconnecting, relocating, and reestablishing the home.
alaska.eviction: Eviction grounds are a closed list in AS 34.03.225(a). An operator may evict only for default in payment of rent, a continuing conviction for violating federal, state, or local law that is detrimental to the health, safety, or welfare of other dwellers or tenants, violation of an enforceable provision of the signed rental agreement, or a change in use of the park land.
alaska.sale: A rental agreement may not deny a park tenant the right to sell the tenant's mobile home within the park or require removal solely because of the sale, under AS 34.03.040(c)(1). Within 30 days of written notice of intent to sell to a specified buyer, the operator may refuse the sale only if the home violates health, safety, or welfare laws or ordinances, the buyer refuses to assume the same rental terms, or the buyer does not have sufficient financial responsibility.

arizona.law: The Arizona Mobile Home Parks Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, Arizona Revised Statutes Title 33, Chapter 11, Sections 33-1401 to 33-1501, governs lot tenancies in mobile home parks.
arizona.rent: On expiration or renewal of a rental agreement, the landlord may increase rent only after notifying the tenant in writing by first class or certified mail or personal delivery at least 90 days before the expiration or renewal, under Section 33-1413(G).
arizona.closure: The landlord must notify the director and all tenants in writing of a change in use at least 180 days before the change in use, and may not increase rent within 90 days before giving that notice, under Section 33-1476.01(A). A tenant who must move may collect from the Mobile Home Relocation Fund the lesser of actual moving expenses within Arizona or a maximum of $22,500 for a single-section home or $30,000 for a multisection home.
arizona.eviction: Termination or nonrenewal requires good cause under Section 33-1476(B), a closed list: noncompliance with the rental agreement, nonpayment of rent, change in use of land, or clear and convincing evidence of repeated violations establishing a pattern of noncompliance with the Act.
arizona.sale: Park rules may not prohibit a tenant from advertising the sale or exchange of the tenant's mobile home, and the landlord may not exact a commission or fee on the sale price unless the landlord acted as agent under a written agreement or require use of a specific sales agency, under Section 33-1452. After a sale, the landlord may require removal within 60 days if the home does not meet current park rules and state requirements.
arizona.link_label: Arizona Legislature - ARS Section 33-1476.01, Change in use
arizona.retaliation: Arizona's park act bans retaliation: under A.R.S. § 33-1491, a landlord may not raise rent, cut services, or bring or threaten an eviction because you complained in good faith to a housing-code agency, complained to the landlord about a violation, joined a tenants' organization, or sued the landlord. If the landlord acts within six months of your complaint, the law presumes it was retaliation, and retaliation is a defense to eviction.

arkansas.law: Arkansas has no separate mobile-home park tenancy act. Residential rentals are covered by the general Arkansas Residential Landlord-Tenant Act of 2007, Arkansas Code Title 18, Chapter 17, Sections 18-17-101 et seq.
arkansas.rent: The general landlord-tenant act does not set a separate lot-rent increase notice period for manufactured-home parks.
arkansas.closure: The general landlord-tenant act does not set a park closure or change-of-use notice period, and it does not set a park relocation-assistance duty.
arkansas.eviction: Eviction grounds are not a closed park-specific list. Under the general act, a landlord may pursue remedies for noncompliance with the rental agreement or failure to pay rent, under Section 18-17-701, and possession through the general unlawful-detainer process.
arkansas.link_label: Arkansas State Legislature - Residential Landlord Tenant Act of 2007, Act 1004 (HB2540)

california.law: The Mobilehome Residency Law, California Civil Code Chapter 2.5, Sections 798 to 799.13, governs tenancies in mobilehome parks and is distinct from general landlord-tenant law.
california.rent: Management must give a homeowner written notice of any increase in rent at least 90 days before the date of the increase, under Civil Code Section 798.30.
california.closure: For a change of use of the park, management must give at least 60 days written notice that it will appear before a local governmental board, commission, or body to request permits, and after all required permits are approved must give six months or more written notice of termination of tenancy, under Civil Code Section 798.56(g). If the change of use requires no local governmental permits, notice must be given 12 months or more before the change, and the relocation-impact report required by Government Code Section 65863.7 must be given to homeowners.
california.eviction: Termination grounds are a closed list in Civil Code Section 798.56. Management may terminate only for failure to comply with a local ordinance or state law or regulation relating to mobilehomes, specified convictions committed on park premises, failure to comply with a reasonable park rule that is part of the rental agreement, nonpayment of rent, utility charges, or reasonable incidental service charges, condemnation of the park, or change of use of the park.
california.sale: Management shall not prohibit the listing or sale of a mobilehome within the park by the homeowner, under Civil Code Section 798.71, and shall not require removal of a mobilehome on sale to a third party during the term of the rental agreement, under Section 798.73, subject to the Act's stated exceptions. Management may require prior approval of a purchaser who will remain in the park, under Section 798.74.
california.link_label: California Legislative Information - Civil Code Chapter 2.5, Mobilehome Residency Law, Article 6
california.retaliation: The Mobilehome Residency Law has no retaliation section of its own, but California's general rule, Civil Code § 1942.5, bars a park owner from raising rent, cutting services, or seeking possession within 180 days after your good-faith complaint about habitability, a complaint to a public agency, or lawful organizing activity — and California courts have applied it to park tenancies.

colorado.law: The Mobile Home Park Act, Colorado Revised Statutes Part 2 of Article 12 of Title 38, Sections 38-12-200.1 to 38-12-221, governs the relationship between a mobile home park owner and a home owner in the park.
colorado.rent: A landlord must provide home owners renting lot space with at least 60 days written notice before any rent increase takes effect, and may increase rent only once in any 12-month period of consecutive occupancy, under Section 38-12-204.
colorado.closure: A landlord must give written notice of intent to change the use of the park at least 12 months before the change in use will occur, under Sections 38-12-203(1)(d) and 38-12-217(1)(b). The Division of Housing rights notice states that if a closure will displace a home, the home owner can give the landlord a written demand for relocation costs or compensation, under Section 38-12-203.5.
colorado.eviction: Termination grounds are a closed list in Section 38-12-203. Management may terminate only for listed reasons including failure to comply with local ordinances and state laws and rules relating to mobile homes and lots, failure to comply with enforceable written park rules, condemnation or change of use, materially false statements on a tenancy application, or conduct that endangers or harms others or property, with nonpayment handled under Section 38-12-204.
colorado.sale: Management shall not interfere with a home owner's right to sell a mobile home in place to a buyer of the home owner's choosing, subject to the Act's stated compliance limits, and selling and transfer fees are prohibited and for-sale signs are permitted under Section 38-12-211. For a park sale, the landlord must provide notice of intent to sell within 14 days of a triggering event, and a group or association of home owners or their assignees have 120 days after the landlord mails that notice to submit a proposed purchase and sale agreement, under Section 38-12-217.
colorado.link_label: Colorado Division of Housing - Notice of Home Owner and Resident Rights
colorado.retaliation: Under C.R.S. § 38-12-212.5, park management may not take retaliatory action against a home owner who exercises any right under the Mobile Home Park Act or any other law. If management acts within 120 days after you complained to an agency or to management, joined a residents' association, or voted on a park-purchase opportunity, the action is presumed retaliatory.

connecticut.law: Mobile manufactured home parks are governed by Connecticut General Statutes Chapter 412, Sections 21-64 to 21-84, Mobile Manufactured Homes and Mobile Manufactured Home Parks - Park Owners and Residents.
connecticut.rent: Rent may not be increased during the term of the rental agreement, under Section 21-83(a)(5). At termination of the agreement, the owner may propose an increase only if the owner delivers written notice of the proposed increase to the resident at least 30 days before the start of a new rental agreement, the proposed rent is consistent with rents for comparable lots in the same park, and the rent is not increased to defeat the eviction protections, under Section 21-80.
connecticut.closure: For a change in use, a resident who owns a mobile manufactured home must be given written notice at least 545 days before the time specified to quit possession if the notice is given on or after June 23, 1999, under Section 21-80(b). A resident who must remove the home because of a change in use is entitled to relocation expenses to a satisfactory park within 100 miles, up to a maximum of $10,000, under Section 21-70a.
connecticut.eviction: For a resident who owns the home, summary process or termination grounds are a closed list in Section 21-80(b): nonpayment of rent, utility charges, or reasonable incidental services charges, material noncompliance with a statute or regulation materially affecting health and safety or the physical condition of the park, material noncompliance with the rental agreement or rules adopted under Section 21-70, failure to agree to a proposed rent increase that meets Section 21-80's conditions, or a change in use of the land.
connecticut.sale: Section 21-79 prohibits the owner from restricting the resident's right to sell the resident's mobile manufactured home, and the rental agreement must state that right. For a park sale to change the land use, an association representing 25 percent or more of the units may notify the owner within 120 days after the required notice is mailed that it is interested in purchasing, and then has 365 days to purchase the park, including by matching an offer, under Section 21-70(f); for other park sales, leases, or transfers, notice must be given at least 45 days before the sale and an association has 180 days to purchase and close, under Section 21-70b.
connecticut.link_label: Connecticut General Assembly - Chapter 412, Mobile Manufactured Homes and Mobile Manufactured Home Parks

delaware.law: Manufactured home communities are governed by the Manufactured Homes and Manufactured Home Communities Act, Title 25, Chapter 70 of the Delaware Code, Sections 7001 et seq.
delaware.rent: Lot rent may be increased only once during any 12 months, regardless of the term of the tenancy or rental agreement, and the landlord must provide written notice of a lot rent increase at least 90 days before the effective date of the increase.
delaware.closure: For an intended change in use of community land, the landlord must provide all affected tenants with at least a 1-year termination or nonrenewal notice, may not increase lot rent after giving that notice, and must provide a written relocation plan and update it every 3 months, under Section 7024(b). Relocation assistance for eligible tenants is provided through the Delaware Manufactured Home Relocation Authority and its Trust Fund under Subchapter V of Chapter 70.
delaware.eviction: A landlord may terminate or refuse to renew a lot rental agreement only for due cause, under Section 7024(a). Due cause means an intended change in use under Section 7024(b) or the grounds for termination under Section 7016.
delaware.sale: The sale, conveyance, or transfer of a manufactured home that the buyer intends to retain in the community is governed by Section 7013, which requires the homeowner to notify the landlord in writing at least 3 weeks before the scheduled sale with the buyer's name and address and the agreed price and terms, and extends to the landlord a right to purchase the home for 1 percent higher than the contract price. For a sale of the community itself, Subchapter IV, Sections 7026 to 7036, gives the homeowner association a right of first offer before the sale.
delaware.link_label: Delaware Manufactured Home Relocation Authority - Frequently Asked Questions
delaware.retaliation: Delaware's park act bans retaliation: under 25 Del. C. § 7019, a community owner may not pursue possession, terminate your agreement, force you to move, or cut services because you complained about a code violation, joined a tenants' organization, or sued. Action within 90 days of the protected act is presumed retaliatory, and a resident who proves retaliation can recover the greater of three months' rent or three times actual damages, plus court costs.

florida.law: Mobile home park lot tenancies are governed by Florida Statutes Chapter 723, Mobile Home Park Lot Tenancies, Sections 723.001 et seq.
florida.rent: A park owner must give written notice to each affected mobile home owner and to the board of directors of the homeowners association, if one has been formed, at least 90 days before any increase in lot rental amount, reduction in services or utilities, or change in rules and regulations, under Section 723.037(1).
florida.closure: For a change in use of the land comprising the park, the park owner must give affected mobile home owners and tenants at least 6 months notice of the eviction due to the projected change in use and of their need to secure other accommodations, under Section 723.061(1)(d). A home owner who must move is entitled to payment from the Florida Mobile Home Relocation Corporation of actual moving expenses to a new location within a 50-mile radius, or $3,000 for a single-section home or $6,000 for a multisection home, whichever is less, under Section 723.0612(1).
florida.eviction: Eviction grounds are a closed list in Section 723.061(1). A park owner may evict only for nonpayment of the lot rental amount, conviction of a violation of federal or state law or local ordinance that is detrimental to the health, safety, or welfare of other residents, violation of a park rule or regulation, the rental agreement, or Chapter 723, change in use of the land, or the other grounds stated in that section, including failure of a purchaser to be approved where the section provides for it.
florida.sale: Restrictions on the sale of mobile homes and the rights of a purchaser are governed by Sections 723.058 and 723.059. For a park sale, including a sale for a change in use, the park owner must give the homeowners association written notice of its right to purchase at the price and terms in the notice, and the association has 45 days after mailing of the notice to execute and deliver a contract to purchase at that price and those terms, with an additional 10 days to meet a lower revised price, under Sections 723.061(1)(d) and 723.071.
florida.link_label: Florida Legislature, Online Sunshine - Florida Statutes Section 723.0612, Change in use; relocation expenses
florida.retaliation: Under Florida Statutes § 723.0615, a park owner may not discriminatorily raise your rent, cut services, or bring or threaten a possession action primarily to retaliate against you for complaining in good faith to a code-enforcement agency, organizing or joining a homeowners' organization, or complaining to the owner about a violation of the owner's duties. Retaliation is a defense in a possession action.

georgia.law: Georgia has no separate mobile-home park tenancy act. Lot rentals are covered by the general landlord and tenant law in Title 44, Chapter 7 of the Official Code of Georgia, and the Georgia Landlord-Tenant Handbook published by the Department of Community Affairs notes that mobile homes are considered personal property unless permanently affixed to the land, so the handbook rules may not apply to them in the same way.
georgia.rent: Georgia law does not set a separate lot-rent increase notice period for manufactured-home parks in a park act. Under the general law, 60 days notice from the landlord is necessary to terminate a tenancy at will, under Section 44-7-7.
georgia.closure: Georgia law does not set a park closure or change-of-use notice period, and it does not set a park relocation-assistance duty, in a manufactured-home park act.
georgia.eviction: Eviction grounds are not a closed park-specific list. Possession is recovered through the general dispossessory process in Title 44, Chapter 7, Article 3, for grounds such as nonpayment of rent or holding over after the tenancy ends.
georgia.link_label: Georgia Department of Community Affairs / Consumer Protection Division - Georgia Landlord-Tenant Handbook

hawaii.law: Hawaii has no separate mobile-home-park tenancy act. Residential tenancies are governed generally by the Residential Landlord-Tenant Code, Hawaii Revised Statutes Chapter 521, which the Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs publishes for landlords and tenants.
hawaii.rent: For a month-to-month tenancy, rent may not be increased without written notice given 45 consecutive days before the effective date of the increase (HRS Section 521-21(d)). For a tenancy less than month-to-month, the notice period is 15 consecutive days (Section 521-21(e)).
hawaii.closure: Chapter 521 sets no park-closure or relocation-assistance rule for mobile home parks. Its closest general rule is in Section 521-71(c): before ending a month-to-month tenancy for voluntary demolition, conversion to a condominium, or change to transient vacation rentals, the landlord must give at least 120 days' notice.
hawaii.eviction: Eviction grounds are not a closed park-specific list; general landlord-tenant law applies. Under Section 521-71(a), a landlord may end a month-to-month tenancy on at least 45 days' written notice, and shorter statutory notices apply for nonpayment and other breaches under Chapter 521.
hawaii.link_label: Hawaii Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs — HRS Chapter 521, Residential Landlord-Tenant Code

idaho.law: Park lot tenancies are governed by the Manufactured Home Residency Act, Idaho Code Title 55, Chapter 20 (Sections 55-2001 through 55-2020), which covers rental agreements, rent adjustments, sales of homes, and terminations in manufactured home communities.
idaho.rent: A landlord may increase or decrease rent only after the lease term expires and only with 90 days' written notice to the residents (Section 55-2006(1)). Increases must be uniform throughout the community, or uniform within the same rent tier (Section 55-2006(2)).
idaho.closure: If the community is taken by eminent domain or the lot-rental operation ceases, the landlord must give affected residents at least 180 days' written notice before the termination date, and may not increase rent during that notice period (Section 55-2010(1)(d)). The chapter states no relocation-payment duty.
idaho.eviction: Yes — during the term of a rental agreement, a tenancy may be terminated only for the reasons listed in Section 55-2010(1): substantial or repeated violation of the agreement or community rules, nonpayment of rent or other charges, closure by order of a government authority, eminent domain or cessation of the lot-rental operation, or abandonment. A landlord must also give at least 90 days' written notice of an intention not to renew (Section 55-2010(2)).
idaho.sale: A landlord may not deny a resident who owns the home the right to sell it on the rented lot, or require removal of the home solely because of the sale, and may not charge a sale commission or fee unless the landlord acted as the seller's agent under a written agreement (Section 55-2009). A resident association formed to buy the community may ask in writing to be notified 15 days before the owner signs a purchase agreement (Section 55-2013A(4)); the chapter gives no right to match an offer.
idaho.link_label: Idaho Legislature — Idaho Code Section 55-2010, Terminations (Manufactured Home Residency Act)
idaho.retaliation: Under Idaho Code § 55-2015, a park landlord may not terminate or refuse to renew your tenancy, raise rent, cut services, or threaten repossession of your lot because you complained in good faith about a code violation, complained to the landlord about the park's condition, rent, or rules, joined a resident association, or hired a lawyer.

illinois.law: Park lot tenancies are governed by the Mobile Home Landlord and Tenant Rights Act, 765 ILCS 745, which applies to leases of a mobile home or mobile home lot in a park containing five or more mobile homes (Section 1).
illinois.rent: The park owner must give 90 days' notice of any rent increase, and no increase takes effect until 90 days after the notice (Section 6(d)). Rent may be increased only on renewal of a lease, with notification delivered 90 days before the lease expires (Section 9).
illinois.closure: If a park owner elects to cease operating all or part of a park, tenants are entitled to at least 12 months' notice (Section 8.5, Park Closure). If less than 12 months remain on the lease, the tenant gets the balance of the lease plus a month-to-month tenancy at the expiring lease rate so the full 12 months' notice is provided; Section 8.5 states no relocation payment.
illinois.eviction: Yes — Section 15 lists the statutory grounds for eviction: (1) nonpayment of rent due, (2) failure to comply with the park rules, and (3) failure to comply with local ordinances and state laws regulating mobile homes. Nonpayment is not a ground if the park has not applied for its license or license renewal and paid the fees due under the Mobile Home Park Act.
illinois.sale: A park owner may not interfere with an owner's freedom to sell the mobile home to a purchaser of the owner's choice, and may not impose a fee, charge, or commission on the sale except when the owner asks the park owner to help secure a purchaser (Section 24). Since January 1, 2025, a homeowners' association also has a right of first refusal when the park is sold: the owner must give the association written notice of the price and terms, and the association may purchase by meeting the terms within 60 days (Section 6.25, added by Public Act 103-766).
illinois.link_label: Illinois General Assembly — 765 ILCS 745/9, Terms of Fees and Rents

indiana.law: Indiana has no comprehensive mobile-home-park landlord-tenant act. The park-specific law is Indiana Code 16-41-27, Health, Sanitation, and Safety: Mobile Homes, which covers licensing, sanitation, ejections, and closure notice for mobile home communities of five or more homes; ordinary lot tenancies otherwise fall under general landlord-tenant law (IC 32-31).
indiana.rent: IC 16-41-27 does not set a lot-rent increase notice period — the chapter contains no rent-increase section. During a written lease term, the rent stated in the lease controls; check your lot lease for any increase or notice terms it contains.
indiana.closure: A community operator must give residents 180 days' notice before closing a mobile home community, under IC 16-41-27-35 (added by Senate Enrolled Act 148 of 2020). That section provides remedies for violations and does not bar the operator from evicting an owner or enforcing a lien before closure; it states no relocation-payment duty.
indiana.eviction: IC 16-41-27-30 lists reasons an operator may eject a person from a community: nonpayment of charges or fees for accommodations, violation of law or disorderly conduct, violation of a state department rule for mobile home communities, or violation of a community rule that is publicly posted in the community. Other eviction procedure follows general Indiana landlord-tenant law (IC 32-31).
indiana.link_label: Indiana Department of Health — IC 16-41-27, Health, Sanitation, and Safety: Mobile Homes and Manufactured Homes

iowa.law: Park lot tenancies are governed by the Manufactured Home Communities or Mobile Home Parks Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, Iowa Code Chapter 562B, which covers rental agreements, rent increases, park rules, sales, and terminations for manufactured home communities and mobile home parks.
iowa.rent: Each tenant must be notified in writing of any rent increase at least 90 days before the effective date, and the effective date may not be sooner than the expiration of the original rental agreement or any renewal or extension (Section 562B.14(7), raised from 60 to 90 days in 2022).
iowa.closure: Chapter 562B sets no separate park-closure or conversion notice period and no relocation-assistance duty. The operative notice is in Section 562B.10(5): rental agreements are for a term of one year unless otherwise specified, and must be canceled by at least 90 days' written notice given by either party; a landlord may not cancel solely to make the space available for another mobile home.
iowa.eviction: Chapter 562B does not limit termination to a closed list of park eviction grounds in the text in effect in 2025. A landlord may terminate for material noncompliance with the rental agreement or with Section 562B.18, including nonpayment of rent after a 3-day written notice (Section 562B.25), and on a shorter track where the tenant creates a clear and present danger to others (Section 562B.25A), in addition to canceling the agreement on the 90-day notice described above.
iowa.sale: A landlord may not deny a park resident the right to sell the resident's mobile home at a price of the resident's own choosing, but may reserve the right to approve the purchaser as a tenant — approval may not be unreasonably withheld — and may not exact a commission or fee on the sale unless the landlord acted as the owner's agent under a written agreement (Section 562B.19(3)). Chapter 562B gives residents no right to purchase the park itself; on a sale, the successor landlord takes the same obligations, rights, and remedies, including under existing rental agreements (Section 562B.16A).
iowa.link_label: Iowa Legislature — Iowa Code Section 562B.14 (2023 Code, rent-increase notice)

kansas.law: Park lot tenancies are governed by the Mobile Home Parks Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, K.S.A. 58-25,100 through 58-25,126, which governs mobile home park landlord-tenant actions (Section 58-25,100).
kansas.rent: Each tenant must be notified in writing of any rent increase at least 60 days before the effective date, and the effective date may not be sooner than the expiration of the original rental agreement or any renewal or extension (Section 58-25,109(f)).
kansas.closure: The Act sets no park-closure or conversion notice period and no relocation-assistance duty. Separately, month-to-month tenancies under the Act must be canceled by at least 60 days' written notice given by either party, unless the written rental agreement provides otherwise (Section 58-25,105(d)).
kansas.eviction: Eviction grounds are not a closed statutory list. For material noncompliance with the rental agreement, or noncompliance with Section 58-25,113 materially affecting health and safety, the landlord must give written notice specifying the breach, with termination no less than 30 days after receipt if the breach is not remedied in 14 days; for nonpayment, the landlord may terminate if rent is not paid within 3 days after written notice of nonpayment (Section 58-25,120).
kansas.sale: A landlord may not deny a park resident the right to sell the resident's mobile home at a price of the resident's own choosing, but may reserve the right to approve the purchaser as a tenant — permission may not be unreasonably withheld — and may not exact a commission or fee on the sale unless the landlord acted as the owner's agent under a written agreement (Section 58-25,114(c)(3)-(4)). The Act states no resident right to purchase the park itself.
kansas.link_label: Kansas Legislature — K.S.A. 58-25,114, Rules and Regulations of Landlord; Limitations (including sale rights)

kentucky.law: Kentucky's park-specific law is the Kentucky Manufactured Home, Mobile Home, and Recreational Vehicle Community Act of 2002, KRS 219.310 to 219.410 — a permit, construction, and sanitation act, not a lot-tenancy act. Lot tenancies are governed instead by general landlord-tenant law in KRS Chapter 383, including the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (KRS 383.505 to 383.715) in the cities and counties that have adopted it.
kentucky.rent: KRS 219.310 to 219.410 sets no lot-rent increase notice period. Under the general law that applies in URLTA jurisdictions, a month-to-month tenancy may be terminated by written notice given at least 30 days before the periodic rental date specified in the notice (KRS 383.695).
kentucky.closure: The Kentucky community act (KRS 219.310 to 219.410) sets no park-closure or conversion notice period and no relocation-assistance duty; it addresses operating permits, construction, sanitation, and inspections only.
kentucky.eviction: There is no closed park-specific list of eviction grounds. In URLTA jurisdictions, general law applies: for material noncompliance with the rental agreement the landlord must give written notice and the agreement terminates on a date not less than 14 days after receipt if the breach is not remedied in 15 days, and for nonpayment the landlord may terminate if rent is not paid within 7 days after written notice of nonpayment (KRS 383.660).
kentucky.link_label: Kentucky Legislative Research Commission — 902 KAR 15:010, Manufactured and Mobile Home Communities (under KRS 219.310-219.410)

louisiana.law: Louisiana has no mobile-home-park landlord-tenant act. The only park-specific provision found is R.S. 9:3259.1, which covers land where three or more lots are available for rent for a factory-built home and requires notice to lienholders when lot rent is 60 days past due; lot leases otherwise follow the general lease law in the Louisiana Civil Code (Articles 2668 et seq., including Articles 2727-2729 on termination).
louisiana.rent: R.S. 9:3259.1 and the general lease articles set no park-specific lot-rent increase notice period. For a month-to-month lease, general law requires notice of termination 10 calendar days before the end of the month (Civil Code Article 2728), which is the notice that ends the old rent term.
louisiana.closure: Neither R.S. 9:3259.1 nor the general lease articles reviewed sets a park-closure or conversion notice period or a relocation-assistance duty for mobile home parks.
louisiana.eviction: There is no closed park-specific list of eviction grounds. Under general law, when a lessee's right of occupancy has ceased for any reason — expiration, termination, or nonpayment — the lessor must give written notice to vacate allowing not less than 5 days from delivery before filing eviction proceedings (Code of Civil Procedure Article 4701).
louisiana.link_label: Louisiana Legislature — R.S. 9:3259.1, Unpaid Rent; Factory-Built Homes; Notification by Lessor

maine.law: Park lot tenancies are governed by the Regulation of Mobile Home Parks; Landlord and Tenant law, 10 M.R.S. Chapter 953 (Sections 9091-9100), including Section 9093-B on lot rent and fee increases and Section 9097 on rental agreement terms and eviction.
maine.rent: An owner of a manufactured housing community must provide notice of an increase in lot rent or fees no less than 90 days before the effective date of the increase (Section 9093-B(1), enacted by Public Law 2025, Chapter 399). The notice must state the amount of the increase and comparison figures for similar communities in the area.
maine.closure: Condemnation or change of use of the mobile home park is a ground for termination only if, for a change of use, one year's notice is given in writing to the tenant — unless the tenant was given notice of the scheduled change of use at the beginning of the tenancy (Section 9097(1)(F)). Section 9097 states no general relocation-payment duty for a change of use.
maine.eviction: Yes — a tenancy may be terminated by a park owner or operator only for one or more of the reasons listed in Section 9097(1): nonpayment of rent, utility, or incidental service charges; failure to comply with local ordinances or state or federal law on mobile homes or parks; damage to the property; repeated conduct disturbing other tenants' peace, quiet, or safety; failure to comply with reasonable written park rules; condemnation or change of use; renovation or reconstruction meeting the section's conditions; terms expressly in the original lease; or three or more violations of the nonpayment, law-compliance, or rules paragraphs in a 12-month period.
maine.sale: A park owner may not unreasonably interfere with or discourage a tenant's attempt to sell a mobile home situated on a park lot, and may not charge a commission or fee on the sale unless the owner acted as the seller's agent under a written contract (Section 9094). When the park itself is for sale, the owner must give written notice of the intent to sell to each mobile home owner and to the Maine State Housing Authority, may not finally accept an offer earlier than the 60th day after that notice, and a group of mobile home owners or a mobile home owners' association has a first option to purchase — the owner must consider its offer made within 60 days, supported by owners of at least 51% of owner-occupied homes, and a matching offer on substantially equivalent terms takes the first option (Section 9094-A, as amended by Public Law 2025, Chapter 394).
maine.link_label: Maine Legislature — 10 M.R.S. Section 9094-A, Restrictions on Sale When a Mobile Home Park Is Sold
maine.retaliation: Under 10 M.R.S. § 9097(1-A), a court may not order your tenancy terminated if you prove the eviction is primarily in retaliation for joining or helping form a landlord-tenant organization or for asserting any right under the park chapter. Maine's general rule, 14 M.R.S. § 6001(3), also presumes an eviction filed within six months of a good-faith code complaint or written repair request was retaliatory.

maryland.law: Park lot tenancies are governed by the Maryland Mobile Home Parks Act, Title 8A of the Real Property Article of the Maryland Code (Sections 8A-101 et seq.), as amended by the Manufactured Housing Modernization Act of 2023, which added Subtitle 18 (Sections 8A-1801-8A-1806) on sales of manufactured housing communities.
maryland.rent: For a rental agreement with a term of not less than 1 year that is offered for renewal for a term of not less than 1 year, a park owner who intends to renew with a rent increase must give the resident notice of the increase no later than 60 days before the existing rental agreement expires (Section 8A-202(i)).
maryland.closure: If the use of the land is changed, all residents are entitled to 1-year prior written notice of termination, regardless of a longer lease term, and the park owner must send a copy of that notice to the local governing body (Section 8A-202(c)(3)). When a park owner applies for a change in land use, the owner must also submit, as part of the application, a plan for alternative arrangements for each resident to be dislocated (Section 8A-1201).
maryland.eviction: Yes — under Section 8A-1101 a resident may be evicted only on the grounds the subtitle allows, which are: nonpayment of rent; a knowingly false statement in the rental application; violation of a law in a way detrimental to the health, safety, or welfare of other residents or the park; and repeated violation of a park rule or lease provision within a 6-month period. A qualified resident who has paid rent on time and is not in substantial violation is also protected against nonrenewal under Section 8A-202(c).
maryland.sale: A park owner may not prevent a resident from selling the resident's home in the park; the owner may reserve the right to approve the buyer as a resident but may not withhold approval unreasonably (Section 8A-602). When the community itself is sold, acceptance of an offer is conditioned on giving each homeowner notice of the offer's price and material terms and giving homeowners, through a homeowners organization, the opportunity to purchase by submitting an offer on substantially similar terms within 60 days of the mailing date of the notice — unless the buyer files an affidavit of continued use agreeing to keep the property as a manufactured housing community for at least 5 years and to limit rent increases for 3 years (Subtitle 18, Sections 8A-1801-8A-1806, effective October 1, 2023).
maryland.link_label: Maryland General Assembly — Real Property Section 8A-1802, Sale of Manufactured Housing Communities (applicability)

massachusetts.law: Park lot tenancies are governed by the Manufactured Housing Act, Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 140, sections 32A through 32S, supplemented by the Attorney General's Manufactured Housing Community Regulations at 940 CMR 10.00.
massachusetts.rent: An operator must give each resident and any tenants' association written notice of a permitted increase in rent or charges at least 30 days before the effective date of the change, or with such longer notice as the occupancy agreement or Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, section 12 requires (940 CMR 10.03(10)). Rent increases must be applied uniformly to residents of a similar class.
massachusetts.closure: Before a good-faith change of use or discontinuance, the owner must give each tenant at least two years' written notice, delivered by certified or registered mail (ch. 140, section 32L(8)). At the tenant's election the owner must pay either the tenant's actual relocation costs or the appraised value of the home (section 32L(7A)).
massachusetts.eviction: Termination is limited to the closed list in ch. 140, section 32J: nonpayment of rent, substantial violation of an enforceable community rule, violation of a law or ordinance protecting the health or safety of other residents, good-faith discontinuance of the community, or, for a tenancy at will, creating a new tenancy at increased rent under ch. 186, section 12. The Attorney General's regulations state a licensee may terminate only for a reason specified in section 32J (940 CMR 10.08).
massachusetts.sale: A community licensee may not impose any fee, charge or commission for the sale of a home in the community unless it contracts with the owner to sell the home, for a fee not to exceed ten percent of the sale price (section 32L(4)). For a park sale, section 32R requires notice to each resident within fourteen days after the community is first advertised or listed and at least forty-five days before the sale, and residents have a right of first refusal to purchase by matching a bona fide offer.
massachusetts.link_label: Massachusetts Attorney General - Frequently Asked Questions About Manufactured Housing Communities
massachusetts.retaliation: Massachusetts' general reprisal law, G.L. c. 186, § 18, bars a landlord from raising rent, ending a tenancy, or substantially changing its terms as reprisal for reporting a code violation, complaining in writing to the landlord, joining a tenants' organization, or going to court to enforce housing law. A notice served within six months of the protected act is presumed a reprisal, and the landlord must prove otherwise by clear and convincing evidence.

michigan.law: Park lot tenancies are governed by the Mobile Home Commission Act, 1987 PA 96, MCL 125.2301 to 125.2350, with just-cause termination rules in Chapter 57a of the Revised Judicature Act, MCL 600.5771 to 600.5785.
michigan.rent: The park statutes do not set a specific number of days' notice for a lot-rent increase. MCL 600.5775(3) provides that the statute does not prohibit a change in rental payments or terms after a written lease for the site terminates or expires.
michigan.closure: A change in the park's method of doing business, including conversion to a mobile home park condominium, conversion to total rental of both site and park-owned homes, or a change in use of the land, requires not less than 1 year's notice to all affected residents under MCL 125.2328a(2), unless a different period is provided by law. No relocation-payment duty was found in that section.
michigan.eviction: A park tenancy may not be terminated unless there is just cause under the closed list in MCL 600.5775(2): unlawful use of the site, failure to comply with the lease or a reasonable park rule, violation of health rules or of a local ordinance, state law or governmental rule, intentional injury or property damage, three or more late rent payments in any 12-month period after written demand, substantial annoyance, failure to maintain the home or site, condemnation, changes in the use or substantive nature of the park, or public health and safety violations.
michigan.sale: An owner or operator may not prohibit a resident from selling his or her mobile home on-site for a price determined by the resident, if the purchaser qualifies for tenancy and the home meets the conditions of written park rules (MCL 125.2328(1)(h)). Age or size of the home may not be the sole basis for refusing an on-site sale (MCL 125.2328a(1)(a)). No resident purchase-opportunity law for a sale of the park itself was found in these sections, so none is stated here.
michigan.link_label: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA) - Mobile Home Section

minnesota.law: Park lot rentals are governed by Minnesota Statutes Chapter 327C, Manufactured Home Park Lot Rentals, sections 327C.01 to 327C.15.
minnesota.rent: No rent increase is valid unless the park owner gives the resident 60 days' written notice of the increase, and a park owner may impose only two rent increases on a resident in any 12-month period (section 327C.06).
minnesota.closure: At least nine months before conversion of all or part of a park to another use, closure of the park, or cessation of use of the land as a park, the owner must prepare a closure statement and provide it to state commissioners, the local planning agency, and a resident of each affected home (section 327C.095, subdivision 1). A resident may not be required to vacate until 60 days after the required public hearing, and displaced residents may be eligible for payments from the Minnesota Manufactured Home Relocation Trust Fund for reasonable relocation costs.
minnesota.eviction: A park owner may recover possession of a lot only for a reason specified in section 327C.09 or section 327C.095 (section 327C.09, subdivision 1). The listed grounds include nonpayment of rent or utilities after ten days' written notice and a chance to cure, failure to comply with a law relating to manufactured homes, rule violations after 30 days' notice, endangerment or substantial annoyance, repeated serious violations, a material misstatement in the application, and park improvements that require removal of the home on 90 days' notice.
minnesota.sale: A resident has the right to sell a home through an in-park sale, and the park owner may not charge a fee for allowing it except up to $25 for processing a prospective buyer's tenancy application; the sale is subject to the owner's approval of the buyer as a resident under stated, reasonable criteria (section 327C.07). When a park is publicly offered for sale, the owner must give concurrent written notice to each resident household, but section 327C.096 states that notice is for informational purposes only and grants no property rights; separately, if a purchaser intends to close or convert the park within one year of buying it, owners of at least 51 percent of the homes have 45 days to meet the cash price and purchase the park to keep it as a manufactured housing community (section 327C.095, subdivisions 6 and 7).
minnesota.link_label: Minnesota Revisor of Statutes - Chapter 327C, Manufactured Home Park Lot Rentals
minnesota.retaliation: Under Minn. Stat. § 327C.12, a park owner may not raise rent, cut services, change your rental agreement, or seek possession as a penalty for a good-faith complaint to the owner or a government agency, for exercising your rights under state or federal law, or for joining a resident association. If the owner's action began within 90 days of the protected act, the owner must prove it was not retaliation — and retaliation is a defense in a possession action.

mississippi.law: Mississippi has no separate manufactured-home park lot-rental act in the official sources checked. Residential tenancies are governed by the general Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, Mississippi Code Title 89, Chapter 8, sections 89-8-1 et seq., which applies to dwelling units generally and contains no park-specific lot-tenancy sections in its chapter list (sections 89-8-1 through 89-8-45).
mississippi.rent: The general Residential Landlord and Tenant Act does not set a park-specific lot-rent increase notice period, and no manufactured-home park rent-increase notice period was found in Chapter 8.
mississippi.closure: The general Residential Landlord and Tenant Act does not set a park closure or conversion notice period or a relocation-assistance duty for manufactured-home parks, and no such park-specific provision was found in Chapter 8.
mississippi.eviction: Eviction grounds are not a closed park-specific list. Under section 89-8-31, a landlord may commence eviction proceedings for breach of the rental agreement or violation of Chapter 8 under section 89-8-13, or for failing to vacate after the rental agreement expires under sections 89-8-17 and 89-8-19.
mississippi.link_label: Mississippi Legislature - SB2461 (2022), creating eviction procedures in the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, sections 89-8-31 et seq.

missouri.law: Missouri's park-specific lot provision is Revised Statutes section 700.600, in Chapter 700, Manufactured Homes, covering a manufactured or mobile home land lease community where tenants who own their homes lease lots for placement of the homes as a primary residence. Other lot-tenancy matters fall under Missouri's general landlord-tenant law.
missouri.rent: Section 700.600 does not set a general lot-rent increase notice period. It does bar a landlord from increasing rent, except for an increase based solely on an increase in property taxes, during the sixty-day period before giving a change-of-use notice or at any time after giving it.
missouri.closure: A landlord of a manufactured or mobile home land lease community must give written notice to all tenants who own their homes at least one hundred twenty days before requiring them to vacate due to a change in use of the property; if more than one hundred twenty days remain on a current lease, the longer period applies (section 700.600(2)). Section 700.600 sets no relocation-assistance payment.
missouri.eviction: Eviction grounds are not a closed park-specific list. Section 700.600(3) states that nothing in the section prohibits a landlord from evicting a tenant with less than one hundred twenty days' notice for any reason other than a change in use of the property.
missouri.link_label: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Revised Statutes of Missouri, Section 700.600

montana.law: Lot tenancies are governed by the Montana Residential Mobile Home Lot Rental Act, Montana Code Annotated Title 70, Chapter 33, which applies where a landlord rents a lot to a tenant for placement of the tenant's mobile home, in a park or on an individual parcel (section 70-33-104).
montana.rent: Chapter 33 does not set a specific lot-rent increase notice period in the sections reviewed; rent terms are governed by the rental agreement under section 70-33-201.
montana.closure: For a change of use of all or part of the premises from mobile home lot rentals to another use, the landlord must give at least 15 days' written notice of appearing before a unit of local government to request permits, and, after permits are approved, 6 months' written notice of termination of tenancy; if no permits are required, notice must be given at least 6 months before the change of use (section 70-33-433(2)). Section 70-33-433 sets no relocation-payment duty.
montana.eviction: Termination is governed by the grounds listed in section 70-33-433(1), each with its own notice period, including nonpayment of rent (7 days), rule violations (14 days, or 24 hours if an immediate threat), repeated late payment, disorderly conduct, convictions detrimental to health, safety or welfare, changes in the use of the land (180 days), and any legitimate business reason not covered elsewhere if the landlord gives a minimum of 90 days' written notice.
montana.sale: A mobile home owner who owns the home but rents the lot has the exclusive right to sell the mobile home without interference or conditions by the landlord (section 70-33-305(3)). The sale does not automatically entitle the purchaser to rent the lot; the purchaser must make suitable arrangements with the landlord and enter into a rental agreement. No resident purchase-opportunity law for a sale of the park itself was found in Chapter 33, so none is stated here.
montana.link_label: Montana Code Annotated - Section 70-33-305, Transfer of premises by tenant (official text published by the Montana Legislative Services Division)

nebraska.law: Park lot tenancies are governed by the Mobile Home Landlord and Tenant Act, Nebraska Revised Statutes sections 76-1450 to 76-14,111 (Chapter 76, Article 14).
nebraska.rent: Each tenant must be notified in writing of any rent increase, by actual notice or by United States mail, at least sixty days prior to the effective date of the increase (section 76-1490).
nebraska.closure: The Mobile Home Landlord and Tenant Act does not set a separate park closure or conversion notice period or a relocation-assistance duty in the sections reviewed. Generally, rental agreements are month to month unless otherwise specified in writing, and a rental agreement may be canceled by at least thirty days' written notice given by either party (section 76-1475(5)).
nebraska.eviction: A landlord may terminate a tenancy only by means of the procedures provided in the Mobile Home Landlord and Tenant Act (section 76-14,104). For material noncompliance with the rental agreement or with section 76-1493, the landlord must give written notice and the agreement terminates on a date not less than thirty days after receipt, with a chance to remedy a remediable breach; for unpaid rent, the landlord may terminate if the tenant fails to pay within five days after written notice of nonpayment (section 76-14,101).
nebraska.sale: A landlord may not deny any resident the right to sell that person's mobile home at a price of his or her own choosing (section 76-1495(3)). The tenant must give the landlord notice of the intended sale, the landlord may reserve the right to approve or disapprove the prospective purchaser as a tenant within ten days, and the landlord may not unreasonably refuse or restrict the sale. No resident purchase-opportunity law for a sale of the park itself was found in the Act, so none is stated here.
nebraska.link_label: Nebraska Legislature - Revised Statutes Section 76-1495, Landlord; prohibited acts

nevada.law: Park lot tenancies are governed by Nevada Revised Statutes Chapter 118B, Landlord and Tenant: Manufactured Home Parks.
nevada.rent: A landlord may not increase rent or additional charges unless written notice advising the tenant of the increase is received by the tenant 90 days before the first payment to be increased, and written notice is given to prospective tenants before their tenancy begins (NRS 118B.150(1)(a)).
nevada.closure: Written notice of any closure must be served on each tenant giving the tenant at least 180 days after the date of the notice before the tenant is required to move his or her manufactured home from the lot, and the same 180-day notice applies after final approval of a conversion to another use (NRS 118B.177 and 118B.183). If the tenant chooses to move the home, the landlord must pay the cost of moving the home and its appurtenances to a new location; if the tenant chooses not to move it, it cannot be moved without structural damage, or no park will accept it, the landlord must pay the tenant the fair market value of the home.
nevada.eviction: A rental agreement may not be terminated except on one or more of the grounds listed in NRS 118B.200: failure to pay rent, utility charges or reasonable service fees within 10 days after written notice of delinquency, failure to correct noncompliance with a law, ordinance or regulation or a valid park rule or to cure a violation of the rental agreement, conduct that is an annoyance to other tenants, violation of valid rules after written notice, a change in the use of the land under NRS 118B.180, conduct that is a nuisance or violates state law or a local ordinance, or, in a nonprofit or housing-authority park, failure to meet age or income qualifications.
nevada.sale: A landlord may not deny any tenant the right to sell his or her manufactured home within the park or require the tenant to remove the home solely on the basis of the sale (NRS 118B.160). For a sale of the park itself, a landlord who lists the park with a licensed real estate broker must mail written notice of the listing, not less than 10 days nor more than 30 days before listing, to any association of tenants that has requested the notice, furnished member names and addresses, and given and renewed at least yearly written notice that the tenants are interested in buying the park (NRS 118B.173); that section gives notice only, not a right of first refusal.
nevada.link_label: Nevada Legislature - NRS Chapter 118B, Landlord and Tenant: Manufactured Home Parks
nevada.retaliation: Under NRS 118B.210, a park landlord may not terminate or refuse to renew your tenancy, raise rent, cut services, or bring or threaten a possession action because you complained in good faith about a building, safety, or health code violation, complained to the landlord about the park's condition or a violation of the park act, joined a tenants' league, or won a ruling against the landlord. Willful harassment of a tenant is also prohibited.

new-hampshire.law: Park tenancies are governed by New Hampshire Revised Statutes Chapter 205-A, Regulation of Manufactured Housing Parks.
new-hampshire.rent: Charges disclosed in writing before the rental agreement may not be increased without an explanation for the increase and a specified implementation date that is no less than 60 days after written notice to the tenant (RSA 205-A:6).
new-hampshire.closure: Condemnation or change of use of the manufactured housing park is an eviction ground under RSA 205-A:3, V, for which an 18-month notice is required. No relocation-payment duty was found in RSA 205-A:3.
new-hampshire.eviction: A tenant may be evicted only for the reasons in RSA 205-A:3: nonpayment of rent, utility charges or reasonable incidental service charges (30-day notice), failure to comply with local ordinances or state or federal law or regulations relating to manufactured housing, damage to the property, or repeated conduct disturbing the peace and quiet of other tenants (60-day notice for these grounds), failure to comply with reasonable written park rules (60-day notice), or condemnation or change of use of the park (18-month notice).
new-hampshire.sale: A park owner may not deny any resident the right to sell the resident's manufactured housing within the park at a price of the resident's own choosing or require removal of the home on the basis of the sale; the owner may reserve the right to approve the purchaser as a tenant, but approval may not be unreasonably withheld (RSA 205-A:2, II). Before a park sale, the owner may not make a final unconditional acceptance of an offer without first giving 60 days' notice to each tenant, with the price, terms and conditions and a copy of the signed offer, and during that notice period the owner must consider any offer from the tenants or a tenants' association and negotiate in good faith (RSA 205-A:21).
new-hampshire.link_label: New Hampshire General Court - RSA 205-A:2, Prohibition
new-hampshire.retaliation: Under RSA 540:13-a, it is a defense to a possessory action that the action was in retaliation for reporting a violation to the landlord or an inspection agency, starting a good-faith action under RSA 540-A, or meeting with other tenants for a lawful purpose. Under RSA 540:13-b, a possessory action, rent increase, or substantial change in tenancy terms within six months of the protected act is presumed retaliatory.

new-jersey.law: Park lot tenancies are governed by the mobile home park / private residential leasehold community provisions at N.J.S.A. 46:8C-2 through 46:8C-21, together with the Anti-Eviction Act, N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 et seq., and, for park sales, the Manufactured Home Park Protection Act, P.L. 2025, c. 362, signed January 20, 2026, amending N.J.S.A. 46:8C-10 et seq.
new-jersey.rent: Under the Department of Community Affairs summary of N.J.S.A. 46:8C-2 to -21, a park owner must fully disclose all fees, charges and assessments before a resident moves in and must provide written notice of any fees, charges and assessments within 30 days before a lease change becomes effective. A rent increase must not be unconscionable, and failure to pay rent after a valid notice to quit and notice of increase is a removal ground only if the increase is not unconscionable and complies with other rent-increase laws and ordinances (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(f)).
new-jersey.closure: Permanently retiring a mobile home park from residential use is a good-cause removal ground under N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(h), and converting a park to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership is a ground under subsection (k). Tenants receiving the related notice may request, within 18 full months after receipt, an offer of comparable housing or park site, and a court may authorize one-year stays of eviction until the tenant has been offered comparable housing or a park site and a reasonable opportunity to rent it (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.11).
new-jersey.eviction: Under N.J.S.A. 46:8C-2, a park owner may evict a mobile home dweller only for nonpayment of rent, violation of a federal or state law or local ordinance detrimental to the safety and welfare of other dwellers, continued violation of park rules after written notice, holding over after the term expires and written demand is made, or termination of the use of the park for mobile home purposes. Removal from a mobile home or land in a mobile home park also requires good cause under the Anti-Eviction Act list in N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.
new-jersey.sale: A park may not deny any resident the right to sell the resident's mobile home within the park or require the resident to remove the home solely on the basis of the sale; the park may reserve the right to approve the purchaser as a tenant, approval may not be unreasonably withheld, and the park may not exact a commission or fee unless it acted as the seller's agent under a written contract (N.J.S.A. 46:8C-3). Under the Manufactured Home Park Protection Act, when a landowner offers the park land for sale or receives a bona fide offer it intends to consider or counter, the landowner must notify the Department of Community Affairs, the municipal clerk and mayor, nonprofits on the Department's registry, and each resident homeowner, with the price, terms and conditions; a resident homeowner group with consent of 51 percent of resident homeowners then has 120 days to execute a purchase contract meeting the landowner's price, terms and conditions, with a financing contingency of at least 90 days.
new-jersey.link_label: New Jersey Department of Community Affairs - Manufactured Home Park Protection Act
new-jersey.retaliation: New Jersey's general reprisal law, N.J.S.A. 2A:42-10.10, bars a landlord from serving a notice to quit or suing for possession as reprisal for enforcing your rights under the lease or the law, complaining in good faith to a government authority about a health or safety violation, or organizing or joining a lawful tenants' organization — and a notice that follows such an act raises a rebuttable presumption of reprisal (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-10.12).

new-mexico.law: The Mobile Home Park Act, NMSA 1978, Chapter 47, Article 10, Sections 47-10-1 to 47-10-23, governs tenancies for space in a mobile home park. The New Mexico Courts explain the Act covers a park with 12 or more mobile homes; smaller parks fall under general landlord-tenant law.
new-mexico.rent: Rent shall not be increased without 60 days' written notice to the tenant. Section 47-10-19 also requires the landlord to disclose a rent increase in writing at least 60 days before it takes effect.
new-mexico.closure: For a change of use that zoning law allows without the zoning authority's consent and that would evict inhabited homes, Section 47-10-5(E) requires written notice of intent to evict not less than six months before the change of use. That section states no relocation payment.
new-mexico.eviction: Eviction grounds are a closed statutory list. Section 47-10-5 says a tenancy shall be terminated only for listed reasons, including failure to comply with local ordinances and state laws on mobile homes, conduct that annoys other tenants or interferes with park management, failure to comply with written park rules, and condemnation or change of use; nonpayment is handled separately in Section 47-10-6 with a three-day pay-or-remove notice.
new-mexico.sale: A park owner may not charge a selling or transfer fee as a condition of tenancy for a prospective buyer, although the owner may apply normal park standards to prospective buyers (Section 47-10-12). Management also may not require a tenant to buy a home from a particular seller or require management to act as agent in a future sale (Section 47-10-11).
new-mexico.link_label: New Mexico Courts - Landlord-Tenant and Mobile Home Park Act

new-york.law: Real Property Law Section 233 governs manufactured home parks (three or more manufactured homes occupied for year-round living), with Section 233-a on sale of parks and Section 233-b on rent increases. It covers a tenant who rents space in a park for a manufactured home.
new-york.rent: No fees, charges, assessments or rental fees may be increased without specifying an implementation date no less than 90 days after written notice to all manufactured home tenants (Section 233(g)(3)). Under Section 233-b, rent increases generally may not exceed three percent unless justified by operating expenses, property taxes or capital improvements, and a larger increase may be challenged in court.
new-york.closure: For a change of use, eviction proceedings may not be commenced until two years after service of the notice of proposed change of use (Section 233(b)(6)). The park owner must provide a court-ordered stipend of up to $15,000 per manufactured home owner, and a warrant cannot be executed until the stipend is paid.
new-york.eviction: Eviction grounds are a closed statutory list in Section 233(b), paragraphs 1 to 6, including holding over after the term, nonpayment of rent after a 30-day written demand, breach of the lease or park rules, and a change of use. Section 233(c) gives the tenant an affirmative defense if the owner does not have one of the listed grounds.
new-york.sale: A park owner may not require a home owner or a later purchaser to remove the home solely because of the sale; the owner may approve the purchaser as a tenant for the rest of the term but approval may not be unreasonably withheld (Section 233(i)). For a park sale, Section 233-a requires the owner who receives a bona fide offer the owner intends to accept or counter to notify the homeowners' association (or all homeowners) and the housing commissioner; homeowners have 60 days to give notice of intent and 140 days to deliver an executed offer matching the price, terms and conditions.
new-york.link_label: NY Homes and Community Renewal - Guide to Real Property Law Section 233

north-carolina.law: North Carolina has no separate manufactured-home park tenancy act; lot tenancies are governed by Chapter 42, Landlord and Tenant, with park-specific rules in Section 42-14 for rental of a space for a manufactured home and Section 42-14.3 for conversion of manufactured home communities of at least five homes.
north-carolina.rent: Chapter 42 does not set a separate lot-rent increase notice period. It does require that a notice to quit for a tenancy involving only rental of a space for a manufactured home be given at least 60 days before the end of the current rental period, regardless of the term of the tenancy (Section 42-14).
north-carolina.closure: An owner who intends to convert a manufactured home community, or part of it, to another use requiring homes to move must give each manufactured home owner and the North Carolina Housing Finance Agency notice at least 180 days before the home owner must vacate and move the home, regardless of the term (Section 42-14.3). If a community is closed under a valid government order, notice is due within three business days of the order; Section 42-14.3 states no relocation payment.
north-carolina.eviction: Park lot evictions are not governed by a park-specific closed list in Chapter 42. They follow the general summary ejectment law in Chapter 42, Article 3, for cases such as holding over, breach of lease conditions, and nonpayment, subject to the 60-day notice to quit in Section 42-14 for manufactured-home spaces.
north-carolina.link_label: North Carolina General Assembly - General Statutes Chapter 42

north-dakota.law: North Dakota has no comprehensive manufactured-home park tenancy act. Park tenant rights on ownership transfer are in North Dakota Century Code Section 47-10-28 (Chapter 47-10, added in 2021 and amended in 2025), with park licensing in Chapter 23-10 and general landlord-tenant and eviction law in Chapters 47-16 and 47-32.
north-dakota.rent: Any month-to-month tenancy agreement in a mobile home park must provide a minimum of 90 days' notice to the tenant before any rent increase is effective (Section 47-10-28(7)). A person who purchases an existing park may not increase the monthly rent for six months if the rent was increased within the 60-day period before the purchase.
north-dakota.closure: Section 47-10-28, the mobile home park tenant-rights section, sets no park closure or conversion notice period and no relocation payment.
north-dakota.eviction: Section 47-10-28 does not set a closed list of park eviction grounds; eviction follows general North Dakota eviction law. A notice of intent to evict a park tenant under Section 47-32-02 must include bold language stating the tenant does not have to vacate immediately and has the right to remain until a court issues an eviction order (Section 47-10-28(10)).
north-dakota.sale: A park owner may not require a tenant who owns a mobile home in the park to sell or transfer ownership of the home to the park owner, except as otherwise provided by law (Section 47-10-28(2)). A person who owns or purchases a park must give tenants written notice of a change of ownership within five business days after it takes effect (Section 47-10-28(1)(d)); the section gives residents no right to purchase the park.
north-dakota.link_label: North Dakota Legislative Branch - Enrolled SB 2159 (Section 47-10-28)

ohio.law: Manufactured home park lot tenancies are governed by Ohio Revised Code Sections 4781.36 to 4781.52 in Chapter 4781, Manufactured Homes (a park is a tract with three or more manufactured or mobile homes). These sections set park operator and resident duties instead of the general landlord-tenant chapter.
ohio.rent: Disclosed fees, charges, assessments and rental fees may not be increased, and rules may not be changed, without specifying an implementation date not less than 30 days after written notice of the change and its effective date to all tenants or owners in the park. No rent or fee may be increased during the term of a rental agreement (Section 4781.40(B)).
ohio.closure: If the park operator sells the park for a use other than as a manufactured home park, the operator must give each tenant and owner written notification of the sale and the date to vacate: at least 120 days after receipt for a tenant and at least 180 days after receipt for an owner (Section 4781.40(A)(3)). That section states no relocation payment.
ohio.eviction: Grounds for an action for possession are a closed list in Section 4781.37: the resident is in default in paying rent; a code violation the resident complained of was mainly caused by the resident or the resident's household or guests; the resident is holding over; the resident violates division rules or park rules; or the resident has been absent 30 consecutive days with the home left unoccupied, without notice to the operator and without paying rent.
ohio.sale: A park operator may not deny an owner the right to sell the owner's manufactured home within the park if the owner gives the park operator ten days' notice of the intention to sell the home (Section 4781.40(H)). No resident right to purchase the park itself is provided in Section 4781.40; a buyer who will keep operating the park is bound by existing rental agreements.
ohio.link_label: Ohio Revised Code - Section 4781.40, Rental agreement

oklahoma.law: Oklahoma has no separate manufactured-home park tenancy act. The Oklahoma Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, Title 41, Sections 101 to 136, applies, and its definitions in Section 41-102 expressly include a site, space or lot leased to the owner or resident of a manufactured or mobile home as a dwelling unit and premises.
oklahoma.rent: The Act sets no park-specific lot-rent increase notice period. For a month-to-month tenancy, Section 41-111 requires at least 30 days' written notice to terminate the tenancy (at least seven days for a tenancy of less than month-to-month).
oklahoma.closure: The Oklahoma Residential Landlord and Tenant Act sets no manufactured-home park closure or conversion notice period and no relocation-assistance duty.
oklahoma.eviction: Eviction grounds are not a park-specific closed list. Termination and eviction of a lot tenancy follow the general Residential Landlord and Tenant Act and the rental agreement, including the notice rules in Section 41-111.
oklahoma.link_label: Oklahoma Legislature - Oklahoma Statutes Title 41, Landlord and Tenant

oregon.law: Manufactured dwelling park tenancies are governed by the Oregon Residential Landlord and Tenant Act provisions for manufactured dwelling and floating home facilities, ORS 90.505 to 90.850. They cover a resident who owns the dwelling and rents a space in a park.
oregon.rent: For a month-to-month park tenancy, the landlord may not increase rent without written notice at least 90 days before the effective date, may not increase rent more than once in any 12-month period, and may not increase it by more than the maximum calculated under ORS 90.324 (ORS 90.600).
oregon.closure: To close a park, or part of a park, and convert the land to a use other than a manufactured dwelling park (other than by eminent domain or government order), the landlord must give not less than 365 days' written notice and pay per space $6,000 for a single-wide, $8,000 for a double-wide, or $10,000 for a triple-wide or larger dwelling (ORS 90.645). The Housing and Community Services Department recalculates those amounts annually for inflation.
oregon.eviction: Park tenancies may be terminated only for the statutory causes in the park sections, including termination for cause under ORS 90.630 for violations of law or ordinance (including material noncompliance with ORS 90.740) and rule violations, termination under ORS 90.632 for disrepair or deterioration of the dwelling, and nonpayment under ORS 90.394. There is no general no-cause termination for a park space in these sections.
oregon.sale: A landlord may not deny a park tenant the right to sell a manufactured dwelling on a rented space or require removal of the dwelling solely because of the sale, may not charge a commission or fee for the sale unless the landlord acted as the seller's agent under a written contract, and may not deny the tenant a for-sale sign (ORS 90.680). Before marketing the park, or when an offer the owner intends to consider is received, the owner must give written notice of the interest in selling to all tenants (or a tenants committee) and to the Housing and Community Services Department; tenants have 15 days to form or identify a tenants committee and notify the owner of their interest in competing to purchase (ORS 90.842).
oregon.link_label: Oregon Housing and Community Services - Park and marina closings (ORS 90.645)
oregon.retaliation: Under ORS 90.765, a park landlord may not retaliate by raising rent, cutting services, serving a termination notice, or bringing or threatening a possession action after you said you would complain to an agency, made a good-faith complaint to the landlord, filed a civil-rights complaint, or asserted any right under federal, state, or local law. Retaliation is a defense to possession, and a violation can support damages of actual losses or $500, whichever is greater (ORS 90.710).

pennsylvania.law: The Manufactured Home Community Rights Act, Act of November 24, 1976, P.L. 1176, No. 261, Cl. 68, governs residents who own a manufactured home and lease a space in a manufactured home community of three or more homes.
pennsylvania.rent: Increases in rent, fees, service charges and assessments are unenforceable until 30 days after notice of the increase has been posted in the public portion of the community office or another conspicuous, readily accessible place in the community and mailed to the lessee (Section 6). Rent may not be increased during the term of the lease.
pennsylvania.closure: On closure of a community in whole or part, the owner must give written notice to residents and tenants, the resident association if one exists, the Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency and the municipality within 60 days of deciding to close, stating an expected vacate date no less than 180 days from the notice (Section 11.2). The owner must pay relocation help equal to the cost of relocation up to $4,000 for a single-section home and $6,000 for a multisection home, adjusted annually for inflation, and at least $2,500 or the appraised value, whichever is greater, for a home whose resident cannot or will not find a reasonably suitable replacement site.
pennsylvania.eviction: Eviction grounds are a closed statutory list in Section 3(a): a community owner may terminate, refuse to renew, or evict only for nonpayment of rent; a second or subsequent violation of community rules within a six-month period; a change in use of the community land; or termination of the manufactured home community.
pennsylvania.sale: Any rule, regulation or lease condition purporting to prevent the sale of a lessee's manufactured home is void; the owner may reserve the right to approve the purchaser as a lessee, but approval may not be unreasonably withheld, and a sale fee or commission is void unless a bona fide licensed sales agent acted under a separate written fee agreement (Section 11). For a sale or lease of the community itself, the owner must give written notice to residents and tenants and to the Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency within 30 days after an agreement of sale is signed (Section 11.1); Section 11.1 gives notice only, with no resident right to match an offer.
pennsylvania.link_label: Pennsylvania General Assembly - Manufactured Home Community Rights Act, Act 261 of 1976

rhode-island.law: The Rhode Island Mobile and Manufactured Home Act, General Laws Title 31, Chapter 44, Sections 31-44-1 et seq., governs mobile and manufactured home parks (a plot with four or more homes occupied for residential purposes), with lot rent increases also addressed in Chapter 44.1, Section 31-44.1-2.
rhode-island.rent: If a park licensee changes the rent or fees for a lot, notice must be given to the resident at least 60 days before the effective date of the change (Section 31-44-3(6); Section 31-44.1-2(a) also requires 60 days' written notice). If a majority of home owners believe an increase is excessive, they may seek binding arbitration, and no increase takes effect until the earlier of completion of arbitration or 120 days after the notice (Section 31-44.1-2(e)).
rhode-island.closure: If a park is to be sold or leased for a purpose that would discontinue the park, the owner must give at least one year of written notice by certified mail, return receipt requested, to each resident (Section 31-44-3.2). The owner must pay relocation benefits of up to $4,000 or the resident's actual relocation expenses, whichever is less, within 10 days of the resident's departure and removal of the home.
rhode-island.eviction: Eviction grounds are a closed list of six reasons in Section 31-44-2: nonpayment of rent, utility or incidental service charges; failure to comply with local ordinances or state or federal law on homes or parks after notice and a chance to comply; damage to the property; repeated conduct disturbing other tenants' peace and quiet; failure to comply with reasonable written park rules after notice and a chance to comply; and condemnation or change of use of the park.
