Termination requires at least 60 days' written notice to remove, or 30 days for nonpayment.
rhode-island.sale: No park owner may deny a resident the right to sell his or her home while it is in the park or require removal of the home because of the sale, and a buyer may be refused entry only for good cause (Section 31-44-4). For a park sale, an incorporated homeowners' association representing at least 51 percent of home owner households must be notified of a bona fide offer the owner intends to accept; the association has 45 days to execute a purchase and sale agreement and 135 additional days to obtain financing, for a total of 180 days to complete the purchase (Section 31-44-3.1).
rhode-island.link_label: Rhode Island General Laws - Title 31, Chapter 44, Section 31-44-3

south-carolina.law: The South Carolina Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, Code of Laws Title 27, Chapter 47, Sections 27-47-10 et seq., governs renting or leasing of residential lots in a manufactured home park in which five or more lots are offered for rent or lease, where the resident owns the home and rents the lot. The Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, Title 27, Chapter 40, also applies where it is not inconsistent with Chapter 47 (Section 27-47-110).
south-carolina.rent: When a tenancy is to continue beyond the original term, the owner must give the resident notice at least 30 days in advance of the effective date of a new rental rate (Section 27-47-420).
south-carolina.closure: Chapter 47 sets no park closure or conversion notice period and no relocation payment. Its Article 7 covers only notification of a sale of the park and rezoning: if a park is sold but continues to operate as a park, the new owner must notify residents of the change in ownership within 30 days after the closing date (Section 27-47-610).
south-carolina.eviction: Section 27-47-530(A) lists eviction reasons - failure to comply with laws governing manufactured homes after written notice and a chance to remedy; repeated conduct interfering with other residents' quiet enjoyment; noncompliance with the rental agreement or park regulations not remedied within 14 days after written notice; not paying rent within five days of its due date; noncompliance affecting health, safety or welfare of other residents or the park's physical condition; a wilfully false or misleading statement in the agreement or application; and taking of the park by eminent domain - but it also adds any other reason sufficient under common law, so the list is not fully closed.
south-carolina.sale: A purchaser of a manufactured home may not become a resident of the park without the owner's approval, but approval may not be withheld unreasonably; the owner has 15 days after receiving the purchaser's written application to notify the purchaser of approval or disapproval, and if the owner does not act within 15 days the application is approved (Section 27-47-440). Chapter 47 gives residents no right to purchase the park itself; Article 7 requires only notice of a change in ownership and of proposed rezoning.
south-carolina.link_label: South Carolina Legislature - Code of Laws, Title 27, Chapter 47

south-dakota.law: South Dakota has no separate manufactured-home park tenancy act in the official sources checked. Lot leases are governed by the general Lease of Real Property chapter, SDCL Title 43, Chapter 32, which contains one mobile-home-specific section, SDCL 43-32-31.
south-dakota.rent: For a month-to-month lease, the landlord may modify the lease terms, including rent, on written notice at least 30 days before the expiration of the month, under SDCL 43-32-13. The Attorney General's guide states the same 30-day rule, and that the tenant may terminate effective the first day of the next month by giving notice within 15 days of receiving the landlord's notice.
south-dakota.closure: If leased property on which a mobile or manufactured home sits is developed for an alternate use, the lessor must give no less than 90 days' notice to vacate and remove the home, under SDCL 43-32-31. That section does not apply where the notice is based on a breach of the lease, and it states no relocation-assistance duty.
south-dakota.eviction: Eviction grounds are not a closed park-specific list. General South Dakota landlord-tenant law applies, including termination for breach or use contrary to the lease under Chapter 43-32 and forcible entry and detainer procedure under Chapter 21-16.
south-dakota.link_label: South Dakota Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division - Landlord and Tenant

tennessee.law: No dedicated manufactured-home park tenancy act was found in Tennessee's official code or agency sources. Manufactured-home construction, sale and installation are regulated under Tennessee Code Title 68, Chapter 126, while a lot tenancy is governed by general landlord-tenant law, chiefly the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, Title 66, Chapter 28, which by its terms applies only in larger counties (population over 75,000 under the 2010 census).
tennessee.rent: The Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act sets no separate lot-rent increase notice period. Either the landlord or the tenant may terminate a month-to-month tenancy by written notice given at least 30 days before the periodic rental date specified in the notice, under Tenn. Code Ann. 66-28-512(b).
tennessee.closure: No park-closure notice period or relocation-assistance duty was found in the Tennessee statutes or official agency guides checked. A closure would proceed as a termination of the lot tenancies under general landlord-tenant law.
tennessee.eviction: Eviction grounds are not a closed park-specific list; general landlord-tenant law applies. Under the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act a month-to-month tenancy may be ended without cause on the 30-day written notice in 66-28-512(b), and tenant noncompliance is handled under the Act's general enforcement provisions, including 66-28-505.
tennessee.link_label: Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance - Manufactured Housing, Consumer Resources

texas.law: Manufactured Home Tenancies, Texas Property Code Chapter 94. Under section 94.002 it applies only to a landlord who leases property in a manufactured home community (a parcel on which four or more lots are offered for lease for manufactured homes, section 94.001) to a tenant for situating a manufactured home on it; it does not apply where the tenant rents the manufactured home itself from the landlord.
texas.rent: Chapter 94 sets no standalone rent-increase notice period; a rent change comes with renewal. Under section 94.055 the landlord must give a notice to vacate or an offer of renewal, stating the proposed rent, not later than the 60th day before the lease expires (or, for a month-to-month lease, the 60th day before the intended termination), and the tenant must reject the new terms not later than the 30th day before expiration or the lease renews on the modified terms. A lease provision raising rent or fees during the term is void unless the tenant initialed it, under section 94.053(d).
texas.closure: A landlord may choose not to renew a lease to change the community's land use only on notice given not later than the 180th day before the date the land use will change, under section 94.204; the disclosure required by section 94.051 likewise states at least 180 days' notice for a land-use change, versus 60 days for ordinary nonrenewal. Chapter 94 states no general relocation-assistance payment for a closure, although a landlord who asks a tenant to leave before the section 94.055 notice period ends must compensate the tenant in advance for relocation expenses, including moving and installing the home.
texas.eviction: Chapter 94 sets its own eviction grounds in Subchapter E. A landlord may terminate and evict for a violation of a lease provision, including a community rule incorporated in the lease (section 94.205), and for nonpayment where the amounts due equal at least one month's rent, the landlord gives written notice the payment is delinquent, and the tenant has not paid in full before the 10th day after receiving the notice (section 94.206).
texas.sale: The owner of a manufactured home may sell a home located on the leased premises if the purchaser is approved in writing by the landlord and the purchaser signs a lease agreement, under section 94.252. Unless the owner has agreed in writing, the landlord may not require the owner to contract with the landlord as agent or broker in selling the home, or require the owner to pay a commission or fee from the sale.
texas.link_label: Texas Property Code Chapter 94, Manufactured Home Tenancies - statute text hosted by Cooke County, Texas

utah.law: Mobile Home Park Residency Act, Utah Code Title 57, Chapter 16. It governs leases of mobile home park space where the resident owns the home and rents the space.
utah.rent: Increases in rent or fees for periodic tenancies are unenforceable until 60 days after notice of the increase is mailed to the resident, under Utah Code 57-16-4(4)(a).
utah.closure: The owner of a mobile home park must send notice by first-class mail to each resident of any planned change in land use or condemnation of the park, or any portion of it, at least nine months before the day the resident is required to vacate, under Utah Code 57-16-18. The owner may not increase rent during the period between that notice and the day the resident must vacate, and the section states no relocation payment.
utah.eviction: The list is closed: a park may not terminate a lease or rental agreement on any ground other than as specified in the chapter (57-16-4(1)). The causes in 57-16-5 are failure to comply with a park rule, repeated failure to abide by a park rule, behavior that threatens or substantially endangers the security, safety, well-being or health of others in the park or threatens or damages property, nonpayment of rent, fees or service charges for five days after the due date, a change in land use or condemnation of the park, failure to enter into a written lease offered by the park, and materially false information about criminal history on a residency application.
utah.sale: A rule or condition of a lease that purports to prevent or unreasonably limit the sale of a resident's mobile home is void and unenforceable, and a park may not restrict a resident's right to advertise for sale or to sell a mobile home, under 57-16-4. The park may reserve the right to approve a prospective purchaser who intends to become a resident, but may not unreasonably withhold that approval, and it may not compel a resident to sell through an agent designated by the park.

vermont.law: Manufactured Home Parks, Title 10, Chapter 153 of the Vermont Statutes Annotated. A manufactured home park is a parcel under single or common ownership or control that contains, or is designed to accommodate, more than two manufactured homes (10 V.S.A. 6201).
vermont.rent: A park owner must provide leaseholders with a minimum of 60 days' notice prior to any rent increase, under 10 V.S.A. 6236(c). Section 6251 also requires written notification, on the Department's form, to the Commissioner and all affected leaseholders no later than 60 days before the effective date of a lot rent increase, and an increase the owner fails to notify as required is ineffective and unenforceable.
vermont.closure: At least 18 months before the closure of a park, or of any lot that will result in eviction or removal of a home, the park owner must give notice of the closure to each affected resident or leaseholder and to the Commissioner by certified mail, under 10 V.S.A. 6237a. Before issuing a closure notice the owner must first issue a notice of intent to sell under section 6242 disclosing the potential closure, and no evictions may be commenced during the 18-month closure period except for nonpayment of rent or a substantial violation of the lease terms; the closure section states no relocation payment.
vermont.eviction: The grounds are a closed list in 10 V.S.A. 6237: a leaseholder may be evicted only for nonpayment of rent, for a substantial violation of the lease terms of the park, or if there is a change in use of the park land or a termination of the park. A sale or change in the form of ownership of the park is not grounds for eviction.
vermont.sale: A resident may not sell a manufactured home in the park without first obtaining the written approval of the park owner, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, under 10 V.S.A. 6236(d). For a sale of the park itself, section 6242 requires the owner to give each manufactured home owner and the Commissioner notice of intention to sell, stating the price, terms and conditions; the owners have 45 days to notify the owner that a majority intend to consider purchasing the park, and if they do, the owner must negotiate in good faith and may not accept a final unconditional offer from anyone else for an additional 120 days.
vermont.link_label: Vermont Legislature - Vermont Statutes Online, Title 10, Chapter 153, Manufactured Home Parks

virginia.law: Manufactured Home Lot Rental Act, Code of Virginia Title 55.1, Chapter 13 (sections 55.1-1300 to 55.1-1320). It applies to a manufactured home park on which five or more manufactured homes are located on a continual, nonrecreational basis, where the homeowner rents the lot (section 55.1-1300).
virginia.rent: Chapter 13 sets no standalone rent-increase notice period. On renewal of an agreement of one year or more, the landlord must give written notice of any change in the terms of the agreement at least 60 days before the expiration date, and a tenant who objects in writing within 30 days may decline to renew unless the landlord keeps the same terms, under section 55.1-1302(C). New section 55.1-1320 (2026) also prohibits increasing annual lot rent at renewal while a locality's notice of zoning, building or fire code violation, or a habitability inspection report, remains unresolved.
virginia.closure: A landlord may terminate a rental agreement of any length due to a change in the use of all or any part of a park, as allowed by local zoning, only by delivering to each tenant, by certified mail, a 180-day written notice stating the termination date and the reason, under section 55.1-1308(B). If the termination is due to sale of the park to a buyer that will redevelop it and change its use, the landlord must provide each manufactured home owner $5,000 in relocation expenses within that 180-day notice period, under section 55.1-1308.1.
virginia.eviction: There is no single closed park-specific list. Section 55.1-1302(D) requires renewal except for reasons that would justify termination or eviction under sections 55.1-1311 or 55.1-1315, with written notice at least 90 days before the renewal date stating the reason for nonrenewal; section 55.1-1311 makes the Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act termination provisions (sections 55.1-1234 through 55.1-1252) apply to lot tenancies, and section 55.1-1315 adds eviction for a building or housing code violation caused by lack of reasonable care by the tenant, a household member, or a guest or invitee.
virginia.sale: A landlord shall not unreasonably refuse or restrict the sale or rental of a manufactured home located in the park, and a refusal based exclusively or predominantly on the age of the home is unreasonable, under section 55.1-1310; an evicted tenant also has 90 days after judgment to sell the home in place, under section 55.1-1316. For a sale of the park, sections 55.1-1308.3 and 55.1-1308.4 (added 2026, effective July 1, 2026) give a resident entity representing more than 50 percent of tenant households, and then the locality, a right of first refusal: the owner must give notice of a sales contract, with its price and material terms, within five business days, the resident entity has 15 days to state its intent (the locality a further 15 days), 60 days to deliver a matching purchase agreement, and 60 days after the agreement to obtain financing and close, with a commitment to preserve the park for at least 15 years.
virginia.link_label: Virginia Legislative Information System - Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 13, Manufactured Home Lot Rental Act

washington.law: Manufactured/Mobile Home Landlord-Tenant Act, Revised Code of Washington Chapter 59.20. It governs rental agreements for manufactured and mobile home lots in manufactured/mobile home communities.
washington.rent: A landlord seeking to increase rent on expiration of a rental agreement must notify the tenant in writing three months prior to the effective date of any increase in rent, under RCW 59.20.090(2). Under the 2025 law in RCW 59.20.370, a landlord also may not increase rent during the first 12 months after the tenancy begins, or by more than five percent during any 12-month period of the tenancy, except as authorized by an exemption in RCW 59.20.380, and rent-increase notices must use the form in RCW 59.20.390.
washington.closure: Closure or change of land use of the park is a termination ground only with twelve months' notice in advance of the effective date of the change, under RCW 59.20.080(1)(e). That subsection also sets paid alternatives in which the landlord provides relocation assistance of at least $15,000 for a multisection home or at least $10,000 for a single-section home, in one alternative together with compensation for the loss of the home at the greater of 50 percent of its assessed market value in the prior tax year or $5,000, with at least 12 or 18 months to vacate depending on the alternative; homeowners may also seek state relocation assistance under Chapter 59.21 RCW.
washington.eviction: The list is closed: a landlord shall not terminate or fail to renew a tenancy except for one or more of the reasons listed in RCW 59.20.080(1). The listed reasons include substantial violation, or repeated or periodic violations, of an enforceable park rule or of the tenant's duties under RCW 59.20.140, and change of land use of the park including closure or conversion, among the other reasons stated in that section.
washington.sale: A tenant's rental agreement is assignable to a person to whom the tenant sells or transfers title to the manufactured or mobile home, and a tenant who sells a home in a park must give the buyer a copy of any closure notice in effect at least 15 days in advance of the intended sale and transfer. For a sale of the community, RCW 59.20.325 requires the owner to give written notice of an opportunity to compete to purchase, before marketing the community for sale, to each tenant, any qualified tenant organization, the Department of Commerce, the local government, the housing authority and the Washington State Housing Finance Commission; tenants acting through a qualified tenant organization have 70 days after the notice to form or identify the organization and notify the owner of their interest in competing to purchase, and RCW 59.20.300 separately requires a notice of sale to tenants and those agencies.
washington.link_label: Washington State Legislature - RCW Chapter 59.20, Manufactured/Mobile Home Landlord-Tenant Act
washington.retaliation: Under RCW 59.20.070(5), a park landlord may not evict you, refuse to renew, raise rent or other obligations, cut services, or change park rules in retaliation for filing a good-faith complaint with a government authority, asking the landlord to comply with the law, suing the landlord, or joining a homeowners association. Under RCW 59.20.075, action within 120 days of the protected act is presumed retaliatory.

west-virginia.law: House Trailers, Mobile Homes, Manufactured Homes and Modular Homes, West Virginia Code Chapter 37, Article 15 (sections 37-15-1 to 37-15-8). It applies to factory-built homes held as personal property situated on real property owned by another in a landlord-tenant relationship, in a factory-built home rental community of two or more homes on a continual, nonrecreational basis (sections 37-15-1 and 37-15-2).
west-virginia.rent: Article 15 does not set a lot-rent increase notice period; the full text of sections 37-15-1 through 37-15-8 contains no rent-increase provision. The notice period the article does set is for termination: a tenancy may be terminated only by written notice at least three months before the termination date, under section 37-15-6(c).
west-virginia.closure: Article 15 has no general park-closure provision, but a landlord of a factory-built home rental community may not terminate a rental agreement or otherwise evict more than twenty-five tenants within a single eighteen-month period unless every tenant agrees in writing to vacate voluntarily, the landlord provides not less than six months' notice to terminate to each tenant, or the tenant has breached the rental agreement, under section 37-15-6a. A tenant aggrieved by a violation of that section may recover actual damages and the costs required to relocate, plus treble damages or one year's rent, whichever is greater, and reasonable attorney fees.
west-virginia.eviction: Early termination is limited to good cause as defined in section 37-15-2(e): the tenant is in arrears in periodic payments or other charges, the tenant has breached a material term of the written rental agreement or repeatedly breached other terms, the tenant breached a material warranty or leasehold covenant where there is no written agreement covering it, or the tenant deliberately or negligently damaged the property or knowingly permitted another person to do so. A single-section home's tenancy may not be terminated until twelve months after the home is placed on the site, and a multi-section home's not until five years after placement, except for good cause (section 37-15-6(a)); after the stated term and those periods have run, either party may terminate for any reason on the three months' written notice in section 37-15-6(c), unless the agreement requires reasons.
west-virginia.sale: The written rental agreement may not contain a provision prohibiting the tenant who owns the factory-built home from selling it, under section 37-15-3(d)(1), and a landlord may not collect a commission on the sale of a home in the community unless the tenant expressly employs the landlord to perform a service in connection with the sale (section 37-15-5(a)(3)). Unless the landlord is changing the use of the site, if a tenancy is ended by the landlord at the later of its stated term or the section 37-15-6(a) period with no good cause, the owner may not prevent the sale of the home in place to another tenant who meets the standards and restrictions in effect for other new tenants (section 37-15-6(f)).
west-virginia.link_label: West Virginia Legislature - West Virginia Code Section 37-15-6, Termination of Tenancy

wisconsin.law: Manufactured and mobile home community regulations, Wisconsin Statutes section 710.15, read with Chapter 704 (landlord and tenant) and the Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection rules in Chapter ATCP 125, which state that landlord-tenant relationships in manufactured home communities are subject to Chapter 704, section 710.15, Chapter ATCP 125 and Chapter ATCP 134. Section 710.15 defines a community as ground on which three or more mobile or manufactured homes occupied as dwellings are located.
wisconsin.rent: Rent and other charges may not be increased during the term of the rental agreement, except for the pass-through items listed in ATCP 125.03(4). If a change or increase in rent or fees, or any other substantial change in tenancy terms, is to be made in connection with renewal of a rental agreement, a copy of the proposed new agreement or amendments must be furnished to the tenant in writing at least 28 days before the date the proposed new agreement is to take effect, under ATCP 125.05(1).
wisconsin.closure: Section 710.15(5m)(f) makes it a termination ground that the community owner or operator seeks to retire the community or a site permanently from the rental housing market. That provision states no separate closure notice period and no relocation-assistance duty.
wisconsin.eviction: The list is closed: under section 710.15(5m), a resident's or occupant's tenancy may not be terminated, and renewal of the lease may not be denied, except on the listed grounds - failure to pay rent, taxes or other charges due; disorderly conduct disrupting others' peaceful enjoyment; vandalism or waste; breach of any term of the lease; violation of community rules endangering health or safety or disrupting peaceful enjoyment, after written notice to cease; violation of laws or ordinances relating to mobile or manufactured homes, after written notice to cease; retiring the community or a site permanently; a government order requiring discontinuance of use; the home's physical condition threatening health or safety or, by its appearance, disrupting others' enjoyment; refusal to sign a lease; material misrepresentation in the application or failure to meet nondiscriminatory application criteria; and violation of a community rule prohibiting a resident from owning more than one home in the community.
wisconsin.sale: An operator may not require the removal of a mobile or manufactured home from a community solely or in any part because the ownership or occupancy of the home has changed or will change, or solely on the basis of the home's age, under section 710.15(3)(b) and (4), so a home may be sold in place; the operator may lawfully screen prospective residents, and the rental agreement must disclose that the operator reserves the right to screen the purchaser of a tenant's home before renting a site to the purchaser (ATCP 125.03(1)(f)).

wyoming.law: Wyoming once had a Mobile Home Park Landlord-Tenant Act - enacted in 1982 at W.S. 34-23-101 through 34-23-110 - but that chapter no longer appears in the current Wyoming Statutes (Title 34, Chapter 23 now covers museum loans), and no park-specific lot-tenancy act replaced it in the sources checked. A Wyoming lot tenancy today is governed by the rental agreement and the state's general landlord-tenant and eviction law in Title 1, Chapter 21.
wyoming.rent: Wyoming law sets no park-specific lot-rent increase notice period in the sources checked, so the notice written into your rental agreement is what controls - read it before you sign, and get any promise about increases in writing.
wyoming.closure: Wyoming law sets no park closure or conversion notice period and no relocation-assistance duty in the sources checked; a closure is handled as an end to the lot tenancies under the rental agreements and general law.
wyoming.eviction: Eviction grounds are not a closed park-specific list in Wyoming. An eviction follows the state's general forcible entry and detainer process (Title 1, Chapter 21) and the terms of the rental agreement.
